text.p: British paper and plastics group Bunzl Plc said on Monday it expects to make continued progress in 1997 even though the first half is likely to show little change from the first six months of 1996.

"We were well satisfied with the record results in a difficult deflationary environment," said Bunzl chairman Anthony Habgood of 1996 results showing a rise in pre-tax profit to 113.5 million pounds ($181.7 million) against 106.2 million.
"We are confident we can continue to progress satisfactorily (for 1997 as a whole)" he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

The strength of sterling and the weakness of paper prices compared to early last year are expected to leave the company's performance broadly unchanged in the first half of the current financial year.
Habgood said fine paper prices in Britain in January of 1997 compared with the same month last year are down 16 percent.

"But prices are no longer falling. They are flat or even up a bit now," Habgood said. "It's (a matter of) just flushing out the effect of the price reduction at the beginning of 1996. It impacts on the first half but it doesn't impact the year as a whole in any significant way."

Similarly with the exchange rate, Habgood said that while it looked like there would be a substantial difference in the value of sterling as far as the first half is concerned, for the year as a whole the effect may be more limited.
"If things stay as they are now we will be looking at a shortfall (for the first half)," Habgood said of sterling at around the $1.60 rate now compared with nearer $1.70 at the start of 1997.
However if the rate were to hold at around $1.59/60 for the year as a whole it would "not be substantially different" from last year's average of $1.57, he said.
Habgood also said the weakness of sterling had more of a 'translational' impact for the company than a 'transactional' one as Bunzl earns much of its profits overseas.
"Therefore, in a sense, the impact is cosmetic but nonetheless real in terms of results. It is cosmetic in terms of it not impacting on the strength of the business," he added.

The group's sales increased by five percent to 1.58 billion pounds. It offered a total dividend of 6.3 pence per share, up nine percent for last year's 5.8 pence, while earnings per share rose to 16.4 pence from 15.5 pence.

The company had sold its European fine paper businesses, Seiler Papier and Bunzl Italia, to the KNP BT Group for 60 million pounds. Bunzl, however, said it remained committed to its fine paper business in UK and Ireland.
Bunzl has also committed around 150 million pounds to acquisitions since the beginning of 1996 and spent 80 million of this during the year.

"We expect that this acquisition programme, combined with continuing organic growth, will reinforce our existing businesses and enable us to continue to progress the group satisfactorily," Habgood said in a statement accompanying the results.
